title.zh: 卷五十九 志第二十八: 食貨上
title.raw: 卷五十九 志第二十八: 食貨上 Volume 59 Treatises 29: Finance and Economics 1

sentences.zh: 食貨志上

translations.literal: Treatise on Food and Goods, Part One
translations.idiomatic: Finance and Economics, Part One

sentences.zh: 契丹舊俗，其富以馬，其強以兵。

translations.literal: In the old customs of the Khitan, their wealth lay in horses, their strength in soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: By ancient Khitan custom, wealth was measured in horses and strength in arms.

sentences.zh: 縱馬於野，弛兵於民。

translations.literal: They let horses roam the wilds and released soldiers among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Horses were turned loose on the open steppe, and warriors were dispersed among the clans.

sentences.zh: 有事而戰。

translations.literal: When there was business, they fought.
translations.idiomatic: They fought only when need arose.

sentences.zh: 廣騎介夫，卯命辰集。

translations.literal: They spread out cavalry and foot soldiers; at the hour of mao they were ordered, and by the hour of chen they assembled.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry and infantry were mustered far and wide—orders given at dawn, all gathered by mid-morning.

sentences.zh: 馬逐水草，人仰湩酪，挽強射生，以給日用，糗糧芻茭，道在是矣。

translations.literal: Horses followed water and grass; people relied on fermented milk and cheese; they drew strong bows and shot game to supply daily needs—dried grain and fodder, the way lay in these.
translations.idiomatic: Horses followed pasture and water; people lived on kumiss and curds, drew powerful bows to hunt game for their daily fare, and carried dried provisions and fodder—the whole economy rested on this.

sentences.zh: 以是制勝，所向無前。

translations.literal: By this they overcame and won; wherever they went, none stood before them.
translations.idiomatic: With this they won their victories and swept all before them.

sentences.zh: 及其有國，內建宗廟朝廷，外置郡縣牧守，制度日增，經費日廣，上下相師，服御浸盛，而食貨之用斯為急矣。

translations.literal: When they had a state, within they built ancestral temples and court halls; without they set up commanderies, districts, prefects, and governors. Institutions daily increased, expenditures daily broadened; above and below imitated one another, dress and equipage gradually grew lavish—and the uses of food and goods became urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Once they possessed a realm, they built ancestral temples and a court within and established commanderies, districts, and prefectural governors without. Institutions multiplied day by day, expenditures swelled, and court and countryside alike grew ever more lavish in dress and display—until the management of finance and supplies became a pressing concern.

sentences.zh: 於是五京及長春、遼西、平州置鹽鐵、轉運、度支、錢帛諸司，以掌出納。

translations.literal: Thereupon at the Five Capitals and at Changchun, Liaoxi, and Pingzhou they established salt-and-iron, transport, expenditure, and coin-and-silk offices to manage receipts and disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, at the Five Capitals and at Changchun, Liaoxi, and Pingzhou, they set up salt-and-iron, transport, expenditure, and coin-and-silk bureaus to oversee revenue and outlay.

sentences.zh: 其制數差等雖不可悉，而大要散見舊史。

translations.literal: Although the gradations of these institutions cannot all be known in full, the main points are scattered through the old histories.
translations.idiomatic: Though the full gradations of these institutions cannot be recovered in every detail, their broad outlines appear here and there in the older annals.

sentences.zh: 若農谷、租賦、鹽鐵、貿易、坑冶、泉幣、群牧，逐類采摭，緝而為篇，以存一代食貸之略。

translations.literal: As for grain and agriculture, rents and levies, salt and iron, trade, mining and smelting, currency, and herd management—gathering each category in turn and compiling them into a chapter, to preserve an outline of the food and goods of one age.
translations.idiomatic: Grain and agriculture, rents and levies, salt and iron, trade, mining and smelting, currency, and herd management are therefore gathered by category and woven into this chapter, to preserve an outline of the dynasty's economic affairs.

sentences.zh: 初，皇祖勻德實為大叠烈府夷離堇，喜稼穡，善畜牧，相地利以教民耕。

translations.literal: In the beginning, the imperial ancestor Junde served as yilijin of the Dadielie Prefecture. He delighted in farming and was skilled in animal husbandry, assessing the advantages of the land to teach the people to cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: In the beginning, the imperial ancestor Junde, as yilijin of the Dadielie Prefecture, took pleasure in farming and excelled at animal husbandry, teaching the people to till the land according to local conditions.

sentences.zh: 仲父述瀾為於越，飭國人樹桑麻，習組織。

translations.literal: His father's younger brother Shulü served as yuyue and ordered the people of the state to plant mulberry and hemp and to learn weaving.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Shulü, serving as yuyue, directed the people to plant mulberry and hemp and to learn weaving.

sentences.zh: 太祖平諸弟之亂，弭兵輕賦，專意於農。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor quelled the rebellion of his younger brothers, stilled the armies and lightened levies, and devoted his mind to agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taizu Emperor suppressed his brothers' rebellion, he stilled the armies, lightened taxes, and devoted himself wholly to agriculture.

sentences.zh: 嘗以戶口滋繁，糺轄疏遠，分北大濃兀為二部，程以樹藝，諸部效之。

translations.literal: Once, because the population had grown numerous and supervisory districts were far-flung, he divided the northern Beidanu into two divisions, setting schedules for planting and cultivation, and the various tribes followed his example.
translations.idiomatic: When the population grew and supervisory districts became too remote to manage, he divided the northern Beidanu into two divisions, set planting quotas for each, and the other tribes followed suit.

sentences.zh: 太宗會同初，將東獵，三克奏減輜重，疾趨北山取物，以備國用，無害農務。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Huitong era of the Taizong Emperor, when he was about to hunt in the east, Sanke memorialized to reduce baggage trains, hasten to the northern mountains to gather supplies for state use, and not harm agricultural work.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Huitong era, as the Taizong Emperor prepared an eastern hunt, Sanke memorialized to cut down the baggage train, hurry to the northern mountains to gather supplies for the treasury, and spare the farmers their labor.

sentences.zh: 尋詔有司勸農桑，教紡績。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter an edict ordered the responsible offices to encourage farming and sericulture and to teach spinning and weaving.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he issued an edict ordering the responsible offices to promote farming and sericulture and to teach spinning and weaving.

sentences.zh: 以烏古之地水草豐美，命甌昆石烈居之，益以海勒水之善地為農田。

translations.literal: Because the land of the Wugu had rich water and grass, he ordered the Oukun shilie to dwell there and added the good land along the Haile River as farmland.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Wugu territory offered rich pasture and water, he settled the Oukun shilie there and added the fertile banks of the Haile River as farmland.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔以諧裏河、臚朐河近地，賜南院歐堇突呂、乙斯勃、北院溫納河剌三石烈人，以事耕種。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict granted the lands near the Heli and Luju Rivers to the three shilie clans of the Southern Administration—Oujintulü, Yisibo—and the Northern Administration's Wenahela, for farming.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict granted lands along the Heli and Luju Rivers to the Oujintulü and Yisibo shilie of the Southern Administration and the Wenahela shilie of the Northern Administration for cultivation.

sentences.zh: 八年，駐蹕赤山，宴從臣問軍國要務。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he halted at Red Mountain, feasted his attending ministers, and asked about the essential affairs of army and state.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, while encamped at Red Mountain, he feasted his ministers and asked them about the essential affairs of army and state.

sentences.zh: 左右對曰：「軍國之務，愛民為本。

translations.literal: Those at his left and right replied: "In the affairs of army and state, cherishing the people is the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him answered: "In the affairs of army and state, the welfare of the people must come first.

sentences.zh: 民富則兵足，兵足則國強。

translations.literal: When the people are rich, then the army is sufficient; when the army is sufficient, then the state is strong."
translations.idiomatic: When the people prosper, the army is full; when the army is full, the state is strong."

sentences.zh: 」上深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply persuaded.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔征諸道兵，仍戒敢有傷禾稼者以軍法論。

translations.literal: That year, an edict summoned troops from all circuits and also warned that anyone who dared harm the grain crops would be dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he issued an edict to levy troops from all circuits, with the warning that anyone who harmed standing grain would be punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 應歷間，雲州進嘉禾，時謂重農所召。

translations.literal: During the Yingli era, Yunzhou presented auspicious grain, and the age took it as summoned by esteem for agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yingli era, Yunzhou presented stalks of auspicious grain, which contemporaries regarded as a sign of the court's devotion to farming.

sentences.zh: 保寧七年，漢有宋兵，使來乞糧，詔賜粟二十萬斛助之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Baoning, when the Han faced Song troops, their envoy came to beg grain, and an edict granted two hundred thousand hu of grain to assist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Baoning, when the Han faced Song armies, their envoy came to request grain, and the court granted two hundred thousand hu to aid them.

sentences.zh: 非經費有餘，其能若是？

translations.literal: Had revenues not been in surplus, how could they have done thus?
translations.idiomatic: Without a treasury in surplus, how could they have done as much?

sentences.zh: 聖宗乾亨五年詔曰：「五稼不登，開帑藏而代民稅；

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qianheng of the Shengzong Emperor, an edict said: "When the five grains do not ripen, open the treasury stores and pay taxes on the people's behalf;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qianheng, the Shengzong Emperor proclaimed: "When the five grains fail to ripen, open the treasury and pay the people's taxes for them;

sentences.zh: 螟蝗為災，罷徭役以恤饑貧。

translations.literal: when caterpillars and locusts bring disaster, suspend corvée labor to relieve the hungry and poor."
translations.idiomatic: when caterpillars and locusts bring disaster, suspend corvée labor to relieve the hungry and destitute."

sentences.zh: 」統和三年，帝嘗過槁城，見乙室奧隗部下婦人迪輦等黍過熟未獲，遣人助刈。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tonghe, the emperor once passed through Gaocheng and saw women of the Yishi'ao tribe, Dilian and others, whose millet had overripened yet remained unharvested; he sent men to help reap.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Tonghe, passing through Gaocheng, the emperor saw women of the Yishi'ao tribe—Dilian among them—whose millet had passed ripeness yet stood unharvested, and he sent men to help them reap.

sentences.zh: 太師韓德讓言，兵後逋民棄業，禾稼棲畝，募人獲之，以半給獲者。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Han Derang said that after the wars, absconding commoners had abandoned their occupations and grain stood ungathered in the fields; he proposed recruiting men to harvest it and giving half to the harvesters.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Han Derang reported that after the wars, fugitive peasants had abandoned their fields and grain stood ungathered in the furrows; he proposed hiring laborers to harvest it and giving them half the yield.

sentences.zh: 政事令室昉亦言，山西諸州給軍興，民力雕敝，田谷多躪於邊兵，請復今年租。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator Shi Fang also said that the western Shanxi prefectures, supplying military expenses, had exhausted the people's strength and much grain in the fields had been trampled by frontier troops; he requested remission of this year's rent.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator Shi Fang also reported that the western Shanxi prefectures, burdened with military expenses, had exhausted the people and much standing grain had been trampled by frontier troops; he asked that this year's rent be remitted.

sentences.zh: 六年，霜旱，災民饑，詔三司，舊以稅錢折粟，估價不實，其增以利民。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, frost and drought afflicted the people with famine; an edict to the Three Departments said that formerly tax money was converted to grain at valuations that were not fair—let them be raised to benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, frost and drought brought famine; an edict to the Three Departments noted that tax payments converted to grain had been undervalued and ordered the conversion rate raised for the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 又徙吉避寨居民三百戶於檀、順、薊三州，擇沃壤，給牛、種谷。

translations.literal: Three hundred households from Jibi Stockade were also relocated to the three prefectures of Tan, Shun, and Ji; fertile soil was chosen for them, and oxen and seed grain were provided.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred households from Jibi Stockade were also resettled in Tan, Shun, and Ji prefectures on fertile land, with oxen and seed grain provided.

sentences.zh: 十三年，詔諸道置義倉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, an edict ordered all circuits to establish charity granaries.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, an edict ordered every circuit to establish charity granaries.

sentences.zh: 歲秋，社民隨所獲，戶出粟庤倉，社司籍其目。

translations.literal: Each autumn, commune members according to their harvest contributed grain per household to store in the granary, and the commune office registered the accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Each autumn, commune members contributed grain in proportion to their harvest, household by household, to fill the granary, and the commune office kept the register.

sentences.zh: 歲儉，發以振民。

translations.literal: In lean years, it was distributed to relieve the people.
translations.idiomatic: In lean years, the stores were opened to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 十五年，詔免南京舊欠義倉粟，仍禁諸軍官非時畋牧妨農。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, an edict remitted old debts of charity-granary grain owed at Nanjing and also forbade military officers from untimely hunting and herding that would obstruct farming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, an edict remitted old debts of charity-granary grain at Nanjing and forbade military officers from hunting or grazing out of season in ways that would harm the crops.

sentences.zh: 開泰元年，詔曰：「朕惟百姓徭役煩重，則多給工價；

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaitai, an edict said: "We consider that when the people's corvée labor is burdensome, then more wages for labor should be given;
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Kaitai, an edict declared: "When corvée labor weighs too heavily on the people, increase their wages;

sentences.zh: 年谷不登，發倉以貸；

translations.literal: when the year's grain does not ripen, open the granaries to lend;
translations.idiomatic: when the harvest fails, open the granaries and lend grain;

sentences.zh: 田園蕪廢者，則給牛種以助之。

translations.literal: for those whose fields and gardens lie waste, then give oxen and seed to assist them."
translations.idiomatic: for those whose fields lie fallow, provide oxen and seed to help them restore cultivation."

sentences.zh: 」太平初幸燕，燕民以年豐進土產珍異。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping, when he visited Yan, the people of Yan, because the year was abundant, presented local products and rare delicacies.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping era, on a visit to Yan, the people of Yan, rejoicing in a bountiful harvest, presented local delicacies and rare produce.

sentences.zh: 上禮高年，惠鰥寡，賜酺連日。

translations.literal: The emperor honored the aged, showed kindness to widows and the orphaned, and granted feasts for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored the elderly, showed kindness to widows and orphans, and granted public feasts for days on end.

sentences.zh: 九年，燕地饑，戶部副使王嘉請造船，募習海漕者，移遼東粟餉燕，議者稱道險不便而寢。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when the Yan region suffered famine, Vice Commissioner of the Household Bureau Wang Jia requested building ships, recruiting those skilled in sea transport, and moving grain from Liaodong to supply Yan; debaters said the route was perilous and inconvenient, and the plan was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, famine struck the Yan region; Vice Commissioner Wang Jia of the Household Bureau proposed building ships, recruiting men skilled in sea transport, and shipping grain from Liaodong to feed Yan—but critics declared the route too perilous, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 興宗即位，遣使閱諸道禾稼。

translations.literal: When the Xingzong Emperor took the throne, he sent envoys to inspect the grain crops of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xingzong Emperor ascended the throne, he dispatched envoys to inspect the grain crops in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 是年，通括戶口，詔曰：「朕於早歲，習知稼穡。

translations.literal: That year, a general household registration was conducted, and an edict said: "We in our early years became practiced in farming.
translations.idiomatic: That year, a general household registration was ordered, and an edict declared: "In my youth I learned the ways of farming.

sentences.zh: 力辦者廣務耕耘，罕聞輸納；

translations.literal: Those who exerted themselves widely tilled and sowed, yet one rarely heard of their paying dues;
translations.idiomatic: Those who toiled diligently in the fields rarely paid their dues;

sentences.zh: 家食者全虧種植，多至流亡。

translations.literal: those who lived off their households entirely neglected planting, and many came to wander in exile.
translations.idiomatic: those who lived off others' labor neglected planting altogether, and many fled as refugees.

sentences.zh: 宜通檢括，普遂均平。

translations.literal: It is fitting to conduct a thorough inspection and registration so that fairness may be universally achieved."
translations.idiomatic: A thorough registration is needed so that burdens may be fairly shared."

sentences.zh: 」禁諸職官不得擅造酒糜谷；

translations.literal: It was forbidden for all officials to brew wine and waste grain on their own authority;
translations.idiomatic: Officials were forbidden to brew wine and waste grain on their own authority;

sentences.zh: 有婚祭者，有司給文字始聽。

translations.literal: for those with weddings or sacrifices, the responsible offices had to issue documents before permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: for weddings or sacrifices, the responsible offices had to issue written authorization first.

sentences.zh: 道宗初年，西北雨谷三十里，春州鬥粟六錢。

translations.literal: In the early years of the Daozong Emperor, in the northwest grain rained for thirty li, and at Chunzhou a dou of grain cost six cash.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daozong Emperor's reign, grain reportedly rained across thirty li in the northwest, and at Chunzhou a dou of grain sold for six cash.

sentences.zh: 時西蕃多叛，上欲為守禦計，命耶律唐古督耕稼以給西軍。

translations.literal: At that time the western tribes rebelled in great numbers; the emperor wished to plan for defense and ordered Yelü Tanggu to supervise farming to supply the western army.
translations.idiomatic: With many western tribes in rebellion, the emperor sought to strengthen frontier defenses and ordered Yelü Tanggu to supervise farming to supply the western armies.

sentences.zh: 唐古率眾田臚朐河側，歲登上熟。

translations.literal: Tanggu led the multitude to farm along the Luju River, and each year they achieved abundant harvests.
translations.idiomatic: Tanggu led his men to farm along the Luju River, and year after year they reaped abundant harvests.

sentences.zh: 移屯鎮州，凡十四稔，積粟數十萬斛，每鬥不過數錢。

translations.literal: He moved his encampment to Zhenzhou; over fourteen harvests he accumulated several hundred thousand hu of grain, and each dou cost no more than a few cash.
translations.idiomatic: He then moved his encampment to Zhenzhou; over fourteen harvests he accumulated several hundred thousand hu, and grain sold for only a few cash per dou.

sentences.zh: 以馬人望前為南京度支判官，公私兼裕，檢括戶口，用法平恕，乃遷中京度支使。

translations.literal: Ma Renwangqian was made expenditure commissioner at Nanjing; public and private affairs were both ample, he inspected and registered households, applied the law with fairness and forbearance, and was then transferred to be expenditure commissioner at the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Renwangqian served as expenditure commissioner at Nanjing, where public and private stores alike prospered; he conducted household registration with fair and lenient application of the law, and was then promoted to expenditure commissioner at the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 視事半歲，積粟十五萬斛，擢左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After half a year in office he had accumulated one hundred fifty thousand hu of grain and was promoted to Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Within half a year he had accumulated one hundred fifty thousand hu and was promoted to Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 遼之農谷至是為盛。

translations.literal: The grain and agriculture of Liao at this point reached their greatest abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Never had Liao's grain production been so abundant.

sentences.zh: 而東京如咸、信、蘇、復、辰、海、同、銀、烏、遂、春、泰等五十餘城內，沿邊諸州，各有和糴倉，依祖宗法，出陳易新，許民自願假貸，收息二分。

translations.literal: Within the Eastern Capital, in more than fifty cities such as Xian, Xin, Su, Fu, Chen, Hai, Tong, Yin, Wu, Sui, Chun, Tai, and the like, and in the frontier prefectures along the borders, each had harmonized-purchase granaries. According to ancestral law, old grain was released and new grain taken in; the people were permitted voluntary loans at two percent interest.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Eastern Capital region—in more than fifty cities including Xian, Xin, Su, Fu, Chen, Hai, Tong, Yin, Wu, Sui, Chun, and Tai—and along the frontier prefectures, each locality maintained harmonized-purchase granaries. By ancestral regulation, old grain was released and new grain taken in; voluntary loans to the people were permitted at two percent interest.

sentences.zh: 所在無慮二三十萬碩，雖累兵興，未嘗用乏。

translations.literal: At each place there were no fewer than two or three hundred thousand shi; though warfare arose repeatedly, supplies were never exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Each store held no less than two or three hundred thousand shi; despite repeated warfare, supplies never ran short.

sentences.zh: 迨天慶間，金兵大入，盡為所有。

translations.literal: By the Tianqing era, when Jin troops entered in force, all was taken by them.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianqing era, when Jin armies swept in, all of it fell into their hands.

sentences.zh: 會天祚播遷，耶律敵烈等逼立梁王雅裏，令群牧人戶運鹽濼倉粟。

translations.literal: When the Tianzuo Emperor was driven into exile, Yelü Dilie and others forced the installation of Prince Liang Yali and ordered the herd-management households to transport grain from the Yanliao granary.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tianzuo Emperor was driven into exile, Yelü Dilie and others forced the installation of Prince Liang Yali and ordered the herd-management households to transport grain from the Yanliao granary.

sentences.zh: 人戶侵耗，議籍其產以償。

translations.literal: The households suffered losses in transit, and it was proposed to register their property for compensation.
translations.idiomatic: Households suffered losses in transit, and officials proposed registering their property to make them pay compensation.

sentences.zh: 雅裏自定其直：粟一車一羊，三車一牛，五車一馬，八車一駝。

translations.literal: Yali himself set the rates: one cartload of grain for one sheep, three cartloads for one ox, five for one horse, eight for one camel.
translations.idiomatic: Yali himself set the compensation rates: one cartload of grain for one sheep, three cartloads for one ox, five for one horse, eight for one camel.

sentences.zh: 從者曰：「今一羊易粟二斗，尚不可得，此直太輕。

translations.literal: A follower said: "Today one sheep cannot even be exchanged for two dou of grain—this rate is far too light.
translations.idiomatic: A follower protested: "Today one sheep cannot even buy two dou of grain—these rates are far too lenient.

sentences.zh: 」雅裏曰：「民有則我有。

translations.literal: Yali said: "When the people have, then I have.
translations.idiomatic: Yali replied: "What the people possess, I possess.

sentences.zh: 若令盡償，眾何以堪？

translations.literal: If I order full compensation, how can the multitude bear it?"
translations.idiomatic: If I demand full compensation, how can the people endure it?"

sentences.zh: 」事雖無及，然使天未絕遼，斯言亦足以收人心矣。

translations.literal: Though the matter came to nothing in the end, yet had Heaven not cut off Liao, this saying alone would have been enough to win people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Though nothing came of it in the end, had Heaven not abandoned Liao, this saying alone would have been enough to win the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 夫賦稅之制，自太祖任韓延徽，始制國用。

translations.literal: As for the system of levies and taxes, from the time the Taizu Emperor employed Han Yanhui, state revenues were first instituted.
translations.idiomatic: The system of levies and taxes dates from the Taizu Emperor's employment of Han Yanhui, who first established state revenues.

sentences.zh: 太宗籍五京戶丁以定賦稅，戶丁之數無所於考。

translations.literal: The Taizong Emperor registered household males of the Five Capitals to fix levies and taxes; the number of household males cannot now be verified.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong Emperor registered household males in the Five Capitals to fix levies and taxes, though the exact numbers can no longer be verified.

sentences.zh: 聖宗乾亨間，以上京「雲為戶」訾具實饒，善避徭役，遺害貧民，遂勒各戶，凡子錢到本，悉送歸官，與民均差。

translations.literal: During Qianheng of the Shengzong Emperor, at the Supreme Capital the "cloud-as-household" registers were assessed as genuinely wealthy and skilled at evading corvée, to the harm of poor commoners; thereupon each household was compelled—whenever interest on loans reached principal, all was sent back to the government, and corvée was equalized with the people.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengzong Emperor's Qianheng era, at the Supreme Capital the "cloud-as-household" registers were assessed as genuinely wealthy and adept at evading corvée, to the detriment of the poor; the court then ordered that whenever loan interest reached the principal, the full sum be surrendered to the government, and corvée burdens equalized among the people.

sentences.zh: 統和中，耶律昭言，西北之眾，每歲農時，一夫偵候，一夫治公田，二夫給糺官之役。

translations.literal: During Tonghe, Yelü Zhao said that among the northwestern populace, each year at farming season one man served as scout, one tended the public fields, and two supplied corvée to the supervisory officials.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tonghe era, Yelü Zhao reported that among the northwestern populace, each farming season one man served as scout, one worked the public fields, and two performed corvée for supervisory officials.

sentences.zh: 當時沿邊各置屯田戍兵，易田積穀以給軍餉。

translations.literal: At that time along the borders garrison-farming troops were established at each place, exchanging fields and accumulating grain to supply military provisions.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, garrison-farming troops were posted along the frontiers, tilling fields and stockpiling grain to supply the armies.

sentences.zh: 故太平七年詔，諸屯田在官斛粟不得擅貨，在屯者力耕公田，不輸稅賦，此公田制也。

translations.literal: Therefore in the seventh year of Taiping an edict said that at all garrison farms the government hu of grain might not be sold without authorization; those at the garrisons were to labor on public fields and pay no levies or taxes—this was the public-field system.
translations.idiomatic: Hence an edict in the seventh year of Taiping: at all garrison farms, government grain might not be sold without authorization; garrison personnel were to work public fields and pay no taxes—this was the public-field system.

sentences.zh: 餘民應募，或治閑田，或治私田，則計畝出粟以賦公上。

translations.literal: The remaining people who answered the call, whether cultivating idle land or private fields, then paid grain per mu to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Other people who answered the call, whether working idle land or private fields, paid grain to the government according to the acreage cultivated.

sentences.zh: 統和十五年，募民耕灤河曠地，十年始租，此在官閑田制也。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tonghe, the people were recruited to farm the vacant lands along the Luan River; rent began after ten years—this was the system of idle government land.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year of Tonghe, commoners were recruited to farm vacant land along the Luan River, with rent due only after ten years—this was the system for idle government land.

sentences.zh: 又詔山前後未納稅戶，並於密雲、燕樂兩縣，占田置業入稅，此私田制也。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered households south and north of the mountains that had not yet paid taxes to take up fields and establish holdings in the two counties of Miyun and Yanyue and enter the tax rolls—this was the private-field system.
translations.idiomatic: Another edict required untaxed households south and north of the mountains to establish holdings in Miyun and Yanyue counties and enter the tax rolls—this was the private-field system.

sentences.zh: 各部大臣從上征伐，俘掠人戶，自置郛郭，為頭下軍州。

translations.literal: Ministers of the various tribes who followed the emperor on campaigns captured and carried off households, set up their own walled settlements, and established touxia military prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of the various tribes who followed the emperor on campaign captured households, built their own walled settlements, and established touxia military prefectures.

sentences.zh: 凡市井之賦各歸頭下，惟酒稅赴納上京，此分頭下軍州賦為二等也。

translations.literal: All market levies went to the touxia; only the wine tax was delivered to the Supreme Capital—this divided the levies of touxia military prefectures into two grades.
translations.idiomatic: All market levies went to the touxia lord; only the wine tax was remitted to the Supreme Capital—thus touxia military prefecture levies were divided into two classes.

sentences.zh: 先是，遼東新附地不榷酤，而鹽曲之禁亦弛。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the newly submitted lands of Liaodong there was no monopoly on wine, and restrictions on salt and yeast were also relaxed.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, in the newly submitted lands of Liaodong, wine was not monopolized and restrictions on salt and yeast were likewise relaxed.

sentences.zh: 馮延休、韓紹勛相繼商利，欲與燕地平山例加繩約，其民病之，遂起大延琳之亂。

translations.literal: Feng Yanxiu and Han Shaoxun in succession pursued commercial profit and wished to impose regulations like those at Pingshan in the Yan region; the people suffered under this, and the great rebellion of Dazhonglin arose.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanxiu and Han Shaoxun, one after another, pursued commercial profit and sought to impose the same regulations as at Pingshan in the Yan region; the people rebelled, and the great Dazhonglin uprising broke out.

sentences.zh: 連年詔復其租民，民始安靖。

translations.literal: For successive years edicts restored their rents, and the people at last grew tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: For years afterward edicts restored their rents, and the people at last grew tranquil.

sentences.zh: 南京歲納三司鹽鐵錢折絹，大同歲納三司稅錢折粟。

translations.literal: Nanjing yearly paid salt-and-iron money of the Three Departments converted to silk; Datong yearly paid tax money of the Three Departments converted to grain.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing paid the Three Departments' salt-and-iron revenue in silk; Datong paid the Three Departments' tax revenue in grain.

sentences.zh: 開遠軍故事，民歲輸稅，鬥粟折五錢，耶律抹只守郡，表請折六錢，亦皆利民善政也。

translations.literal: By precedent at Kaiyuan Army, the people paid yearly taxes with each dou of grain converted at five cash; Yelü Mozhi, guarding the commandery, memorialized requesting conversion at six cash—these too were all policies that benefited the people.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent at Kaiyuan Army, yearly taxes were collected with each dou of grain valued at five cash; when Yelü Mozhi governed the commandery, he memorialized to raise the rate to six cash—all policies that served the people's welfare.
